newsitem.title: USA: Doctors, scientists, teachers top prestige poll.
newsitem.headline: Doctors, scientists, teachers top prestige poll.

text.p: Doctors, scientists, teachers, engineers and members of the clergy are the most prestigious occupations in the eyes of Americans, according to a Harris Poll released on Sunday.
They are followed by police officers, military officers and -- in a finding that may surprise some -- members of Congress.
At the bottom of the prestige list are union leaders, entertainers, athletes, artists and accountants, said the survey of 1,006 adults taken between March 26 and April 1.

Harris has been sounding out Americans on how they perceive occupations in terms of prestige since 1977. During that time, teachers have enjoyed the biggest boost. The level of Americans who believe teachers have "very great" prestige has surged to 49 percent from 29 percent.

By contrast, those who think lawyers have "very great" prestige has tumbled to 19 percent from 36 percent during the two-decade period. Similarly, the reading for scientists has fallen to 51 percent from 66 percent.

The Harris Poll noted that "prestige" was very different from "confidence." Americans for several years have voiced low levels of confidence in members of Congress and lawyers, and more confidence in people who head big businesses.
On the prestige ladder, lawyers, members of Congress and business leaders are in the middle of the pack.

The poll also noted that while many young people view athletes and entertainers as among the most glamorous and attractive personalties, that does not translate into what people view as high levels of prestige.
